title: Poor maternal nutrition programmes a pro-atherosclerotic phenotype in ApoE-/- mice.
ehr_evidence: Experimental animal model using pregnant ApoE− / − mice and their male offspring.
summary: Experimental study investigating the effect of maternal low-protein diet on atherosclerotic lesion development and progression in 6-month-old male ApoE− / − mice.
key_findings: LP offspring had significantly greater total plaque area per animal compared with controls (P<0.05).
LP offspring had significantly greater total cholesterol cleft containing area (P<0.05).
LP offspring showed significantly reduced vascular smooth muscle cell content (SMA staining: control 5.7%, LP 2.8%, P<0.05).
DNA damage marker p-H2AX was significantly increased in plaques of LP offspring (control 14, LP 36 cells/100,000 μm2, P<0.05).
Total and LDL-cholesterol levels were significantly higher in LP offspring (Total: control 6.73±1.01, LP 9.77±0.78 mmol/l, P<0.05; LDL: control 4.62±0.70, LP 8.65±0.70 mmol/l, P<0.01).
HMG-CoA reductase expression was significantly increased in the livers of LP offspring (P<0.05).
No significant differences were observed in HDL-cholesterol, triacylglycerol, non-esterified fatty acids, fasting glucose, Mac3, or p-ATM between groups.
population: male ApoE− / − mice at 6 months of age
limitations: animal model may not fully replicate human pathophysiology
mechanisms linking in utero exposure to atherosclerosis require further elucidation
